issues.body: run_aux_arms caps deeper requests at candidates.max(graph.dict.len()), but check_arm_ids deliberately accepts inline-integer IDs that are not bounded by dict.len(), and derive_mask may contain such IDs when ?node is constrained through an object position. An arm can rank more than dict.len() valid inline IDs before an admissible inline ID; the loop then stops at want >= ceiling without reaching it. The termination argument says entity arms do not rank inline literals, but neither ArmFn nor the vec:hybrid subject contract enforces that restriction. Thus the implementation still does not generally return the arm's top candidates over the admissible domain it documents.
issues.fix_hint: Do not use graph.dict.len() as an exhaustion bound while inline IDs are accepted. Prefer a paging protocol with explicit exhaustion/cursor semantics, or pass the admissibility constraint into the arm. Alternatively, enforce and document that auxiliary hits must be stored entity IDs and reject inline IDs. Add a filtered-ann query-path test whose admissible node is an inline integer bound in object position and lies beyond the current dictionary-length request ceiling.
issues.title: Dictionary-length paging ceiling can lose admissible inline IDs

verdict.summary: Round 3 fixes the prior post-truncation masking defect for ordinary dictionary-backed IDs by paging prefix-consistent arms and adds a meaningful below-first-page query-path witness. However, the paging ceiling is graph.dict.len() even though the same implementation explicitly accepts inline-integer IDs outside that stored dictionary domain. A filtered hybrid arm may therefore stop before reaching an admissible inline-integer hit, so the claimed admissible-domain ranking is still incomplete. This is a new boundary defect relative to round 2, so progress is regressing.
